title: Embedding preserves protocol output
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be the input types of Alice and Bob, let $\alpha$ be an output type, and let $p$ be a deterministic binary two-party communication protocol producing values in $\alpha$. Regard $p$ as a finite-message protocol by treating each of its Boolean messages as an element of the two-element type. Then for all inputs $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$, executing this embedded finite-message protocol on $x$ and $y$ yields the same value in $\alpha$ as executing $p$ directly on $x$ and $y$.
hypotheses_covered: binary protocol p over inputs X (Alice), Y (Bob), output type α
replaced:
For every binary protocol $p$ and inputs $x : X$, $y : Y$,
$(\texttt{ofProtocol}\,p).\mathrm{run}\,x\,y = p.\mathrm{run}\,x\,y$.
